for_you_if: you love demanding platforming and precise combat
you appreciate stunning hand-drawn art and atmospheric music
not_for_you_if: you dislike punishing boss runbacks and brutal difficulty spikes
you find strict healing mechanics frustrating

cohorts.summary: Early explorers praise the visual presentation while wrestling with harsh enemy damage and rigid healing.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe many basic enemies and boss encounters dealing two masks of damage from contact or attacks.

citations.review_text:
Silksong's story and world are incredibly intriguing, and Hornet's kit is alot more versatile than the original game.

However its really soured by several combat mechanics that are more tedious than actually challenging. There are far too many basic enemies that fly, throw projectiles, have too much health, and do two masks of damage. There are so many encounters that are basically a tiny room with one big enemy and several flying enemies that force you to spam jump and dash so much that my finger is about to snap off.

I highly [b][u]RECOMMEND MODDING THE GAME[/u][/b] specifically to reduce the amount of damage basic enemies do and also skip runbacks. There's alotta [u][b]CHEAP PADDING DIFFICULTY THAT WASTES THE PLAYER'S TIME[/b][/u], and I'm not gonna feel bad about skipping it. Still a cool game tho.

I don't think I'm going to finish Silksong. I was a huge fan of Hollow Knight, a huge fan of tough combat games -- Sekiro is one of my favorite games of all time -- and Silksong simply does not care to actually give you a true challenge of skill. Many of the bosses rely on RNG for positioning and attacks, which very often puts you in unwinnable situations, so instead of learning to master your skills, you just try and try and try again until the random selection allows you to win. 

Instead of creating a game with its own unique spin-off identity, they just went "Hollow Knight, but way, way way way waywaywaywaywaywaywayway harder" as if that could ever have been a good idea. 

Enemies do 2 damage now instead of 1. Matters a lot when you have 5 hp to start with. 

Many enemies are glitched and will double- or triple-hit within a few frames, resulting in instant death from max health (assuming you don't have a ton of mask upgrades). 

The game STILL has nonsensical contact damage, one of the worst possible designs in all game design ever, AND random positioning. Many of the hit/hurtboxes do not align with the enemy art, and you will often be killed by two anti-aliased pixels touching the stretched hitbox of an enemy. There's even a boss who has half their body desaturated, darkened, and placed in the background, a very specific visual signifier that it is not an interactable object-- and it does 2 masks of contact damage!

Silksong is not about giving you an adventure, or you learning or growing as a player. It is about making sure you have the most frustrating, least fun time imaginable while in the game. 

Why was it designed this way? Why was it designed to just be a punishing, unfun experience? 

I love the world, the characters, the plot seems utterly fascinating, but it's just not worth it to slog through another RNG based fight, another boss with a faster-than-human-reaction-time telegraph, another glitched hitbox. It's not worth it.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that healing requires a full charge before it can be used during combat.

citations.review_text:
It's the same fun storytelling with gothic bugs, but the gameplay has a somewhat altered rhythm. Hollow Knight felt like it was more about fast, precise responses. Battles were largely singular, and combat flows smoothest once you know how to react to various patterns. Once you've got those down, you can be swift and get in damage. 
With Silksong, they definitely went out of their way to alter the cadence of the fights. There's still that basic DNA where you check patterns and retaliate, but bosses tend to have more adds and projectiles - moves that deny space and force you to be more mindful of your positioning. Attacks are also a bit more subdued - not as mash-heavy, but with a steady rhythm - which might tie into the musical themes of the game. 
Where the Knight was like fighting like a wild animal, Silksong is more measured. 
Some of the restraints may feel heavy, though - like down attack going diagonal and healing requiring a full charge before it can be used. If you try to play with the same recklessness of Hollow Knight, you'll likely get punished until you grasp the difference. 

Still a great game, though. And a great sequel.

I spent over 100 hours playing the Hollow Knight. The level design was incredibly fun, and the combat felt smooth and responsive.

However, Siklsong just doesn't feel as smooth to control as Hollow Knight. Regular enemies feel strangely overtuned, many areas are filled with unnecessary platforming sections, and there are way too many scythes dropping out of nowhere. All of this adds up to a really frustrating and unpleasant gameplay experience.

claims.claim: Reviewers praise the game's detailed hand-drawn art style, visual environments, and soundtrack.

citations.review_text:
**Hollow Knight: Silksong** is easily one of my most anticipated games. The road to its release has been incredibly long, with years of waiting, delays, and very little official news. There were honestly times when I thought the game might never come out. After waiting for so long, finally seeing it become a reality feels incredibly exciting.

What impressed me the most is that the long development doesn't seem to have hurt the game's quality at all. Instead, everything shown so far suggests that Team Cherry has maintained the same level of care and attention that made the original Hollow Knight so special. The environments are just as breathtaking as before, filled with beautiful hand-drawn art, vibrant colors, and unforgettable atmosphere. Every area looks like it has been crafted with incredible detail.

The gameplay also looks fantastic. Movement appears even smoother than the original, with Hornet's faster and more agile combat style creating a fresh experience while still feeling familiar. The platforming, combat, and exploration all look fluid and satisfying, making every encounter exciting.

I'm also looking forward to discovering the new world, enemies, bosses, and soundtrack. If the final game delivers what has been shown so far, I believe it will once again become one of the greatest Metroidvania games ever made.

After such a long and difficult journey, my expectations for **Hollow Knight: Silksong** are higher than ever. I truly hope the wait will be worth it, and from everything I've seen so far, I believe it will be.


『Hollow Knight: Silksong』は、私がこれまで最も発売を楽しみにしてきたゲームの一つです。発表されてから発売まで本当に長い時間がかかり、その間は延期や情報不足が続き、「もう発売されないのではないか」と思ったことも正直ありました。それでも再び発売が決まり、本当に嬉しく思っています。

長い開発期間があったにもかかわらず、公開されている映像を見る限り、ゲームの完成度はまったく損なわれていません。美しい手描きの背景や幻想的な世界観は前作と同じように魅力的で、むしろさらに進化しているように感じます。どのステージも細部まで丁寧に作り込まれており、探索するだけでも楽しそうです。

ホーネットならではの素早いアクションも非常に魅力的です。前作よりもスピード感のある戦闘や移動が楽しめそうで、操作性もさらに洗練されている印象を受けました。探索、アクション、ボス戦のすべてに期待しています。

これだけ長い道のりを経ても、作品の美しさやゲーム性はまったく失われておらず、…

[h1]Otherwise a Masterpiece Undermined By Weird and Boring Metroidvania Elements[/h1]

The combat, gameplay pace and difficulty are great for the most part, and the build crafting options are okay too thanks to different stances and items. On top of that, the atmosphere, art style and sound design are incredible. The strongest aspects are easily the boss fights, core combat, art style, atmosphere, music and vibes.

Unfortunately, traversing the map gets boring fast. New movement options are introduced way too slowly in my opinion, and the biggest issue by far is the fast travel system and the metroidvania structure of the game. A metroidvania should be fun to revisit locations and traverse through the map multiple times, but Silksong fails at that and it weakens its strongest aspects in the process. Going from point A to B really feels like a chore, and I want to reiterate this, it shouldn't feel like this, especially in a metroidvania. Most of the game feels like filler between set pieces such as central levels and boss fights, and the gameplay loop boils down to a checklist tracking where to go next, what to do next type of thing.

One of the biggest negatives is that some secret paths lead to pretty much nothing or very small things, so the sense of discovery is never a strong suit of the game even though genre wise, it should be. Some encounters are not hard on paper, but just go on for way too long to create some artificial difficulty. I found those sections extremely boring because they were basically a battle of attrition against basic enemies. So even though the encounter design is good overall, there are some very sharp exceptions.

In the end, Silksong feels like "you've had your fun for this session, you need to earn your next share so go do some busy work until you can have some more fun" and that's just sad. cohorts.summary: Mid-game adventurers celebrate the soundtrack and world design while debating the severity of boss runbacks and difficulty.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as significantly more difficult than its predecessor, requiring players to master movement and boss patterns from the early hours.

citations.review_text:
You will curse, you will rage, you will want to tear out your viscera in frustration - and you will experience one of the most beautiful and perfectly crafted games made. Completing Silksong doesn't just feel fulfilled, it feels earned.
Whilst not perhaps Team Cherry's magnum opus, it shines in new and wonderful ways.

I would heavily recommend playing Hollow Knight first if you haven't already. Whilst not essential to completion - knowledge of HK-style core movement mechanics is key to alleviating the shock of a fairly punishing early game, not to mention understanding key story implications.

Don't miss out - buy it now.

I recommend this only to the hardcore metroidvania fans. I dont need to talk about graphics / music or technical perfomance here. Everthing is executed on the highest level. Its a great game but there are design decisions that dont work for me personally. This game suffers heavily from developers blindness. They probably played the game for 5+ years during development and cant tell what is hard or easy for someone experiencing the game for the first time. It invokes skills that you only develop after hours in the game way too early. 

This concept is woven trough most parts of the game. Usually metroidvania get easier if you unlock more abilities and tools. In Silksong if you unlock something new you get tested immediatly and need to master it. Somethin like pogo jumping is totally enjoyable after 20 hours in the game, but the first 5 where you need to learn it are a bad experience. I want my metroidvania to be focused on exploration and collecting. 

Difficulty can be fun and rewarding, but Hollow Knight didnt need this soulslike injection. The bad part here is not that you need to learn boss patterns. Its the part that comes before even reaching the arena. The checkpoints (benches) are often in a spot that requires you to do hard movement puzzles or fight multiple enemies on the way to the boss. The ratio of progressing the boss mechanics and even reaching the boss is very frustrating. Sometimes there is no bench after the boss, so you die and need to walk up to the point again. Normal enemies are coded to dodge your initial attack, this gets annoying really fast. Even at the beginning you have enemies hitting you for two life point and you only have five for a long time. No invincibility frames while dodging. The nail upgrades are crucial to progress to the mid and lategame, but pretty hard to find and get. I often had the feeling that the game is not testing my skills, but my patience. Every other room has a breakable secret path, what takes away from the discov…

Hollow Knight was great, Silksong is even better. It's also a lot harder and certainly more complex but it's a pretty elegant evolution of the formula. The world is quite beautiful, the music is great, the bosses are quite fun even if they can be somewhat frustrating, but I'm playing this through again now on Steam and for the most part replaying the bosses has been pretty enjoyable. Some areas of this game are absolutely not fun, but on the whole, I love it.

Silksong, without a doubt, is the best Metroidvania game released so far. It's intuitive combat and movement allow for a fantastic experience that ended up feeling like a dance while playing. The music is just so GOOD! The way the music paces itself to the speed of the combat, and changes inline to the phase just FEELS SO GOOD! The story is incredible, I really enjoyed the world building and all the npc dialogue. The game left me ravenous for more info on the world and its lore. This game is rather difficult, the first game very much feels like a tutorial in comparison, which isn't a bad measure by any means. I would definitely recommend playing Hollow Knight before Silksong. Love seeing work coming out of my home town (Radelaide) getting the attention and acclaim it deserves. Genuinely thank you to Team Cherry for this Masterpiece.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that returning to boss arenas involves lengthy and punishing runbacks featuring platforming segments or multiple enemies along the way.

It's really good and beautiful + a lot of content if you don't miss anything and go for 100%,
BUTt having to make that Sisyphean trek back to the boss every time I die (not to mention waiting for the cutscene or fight right before the boss) ngl kills me more than anything else in this game - DAMN i hate this

ive been waiting so long for this and im disapointed for a few reasons, the first of which is that the bosses are way worse then hollow knight, and the ones that are good are easy, like grandmother silk and pale child or whatever shes called. the second reason is that the runbacks are more annoying by a long shot throughtout the entire game. what i do think is much better then hollow knight here is the exploration, which was fun and all but i care about the combat much more and was disapointed by the enemies

i only got to halfway throught act 3 at the time of this post ill edit if i change my mind, that is if i continue

sorry this review is badly written

Overall, I'd say this game is about an 6/10. It's absolutely beautiful, the concepts are creative, the NPCs are interesting and provide fascinating lore/dialogue, and there is a wide array of equipment you can discover and use at your own disposal. 
Good luck using them, though, because this game is hard as ♥♥♥♥. The enemies have wildly unpredictable behavior; on top of this many of them deal 2 masks of damage and have an enormous amount of health. The boss fights are also extremely lengthy.  I catch myself running out of shards to make tools way too often, especially during bosses and arenas (summons and arena enemies don't drop shards). Some of the runbacks are down-right punishing, too. 
I find it hard to want to play this game. I can only play it like once a month because it starts to annoy me. For comparison, Silksong is harder than the Elden Ring DLC on max NG+.

claims.claim: Reviewers praise the game's soundtrack and visual art style.

citations.review_text: Gorgeous and challenging, with an amazing soundtrack.

Never have I been more excited for a game like I have been for Silksong. It's everything I didn't know I would need, the combat, the music, the art, the lore--it's just so beautiful. I've been a big HK dweeb ever since I've first discovered it's existence, and Silksong only strengthens that dorkiness.

Although it can be a difficult game, I honestly enjoy that! I love the platforming sections, and the bosses are always a blast, even if I spend hours screaming into my screen. The different mechanics we're also intimating at first glance, but I pushed past the discomfort and ended up liking what I was presented with.

THE MUSIC--I CANNOT EXPRESS HOW MANY EARGASMS I'VE HAD WHILE PLAYING THIS GAME. Christopher Larkin never disappointed me with his score, in HK, and yet again in Silksong. The art and details in the game is breathtaking as well, as an artist, I praise Team Cherry and their beautiful unique art style.

I'm very excited for what's to come when Sea of the Sorrows arrive--Thank you, Team Cherry, for giving us the opportunity to peer into this buggy world.

Hollow Knight: Silksong is a stunning sequel that expands on everything fans loved about the original. The game features fast-paced, satisfying combat with Hornet, a beautifully crafted world full of secrets, and challenging boss fights that reward skill and patience. Its hand-drawn art style and atmospheric soundtrack create an unforgettable experience from beginning to end. While the difficulty can be demanding and some quests are intentionally cryptic, these elements add to the sense of discovery and accomplishment. Overall, *Hollow Knight: Silksong* is an exceptional Metroidvania that delivers an unforgettable adventure and stands as one of the strongest entries in the genre.

I don't usually write reviews for the games I play, but this one truly deserves one. The soundtrack is absolutely amazing, and the art style is the best I've ever seen in a game. After 34 hours of playtime, I can confidently say it's a challenging game, especially if you're aiming for 100% completion.
